unit.unitinstructions:
Consent to Participate

You are being invited to participate in a research study. The purpose of this research is to explore how category similarity, spacing intervals, and block size influence bird category learning. You will be randomly assigned to learn bird categories with either high or low similarity and either wide or narrow spacing. Then you will learn bird categories with different block sizes. You have been invited to participate because you are an experienced Amazon Turk worker. You will be one of 200 subjects taking part in this research.

If you agree to participate, You will be asked to complete the following procedures, which typically take approximately one hour. It is important to note that you should complete these procedures within two hours.


           1. You will complete a pretest consisting of 40 items. Each item will display a bird image, and you need to select the corresponding category for the bird. There will be no feedback provided for your answers.

          2. You will progress to a learning session encompassing 168 trials. Similar to the pretest, your task will be to correctly categorize each bird for every trial. You will receive feedback on your responses to facilitate your learning process. In the event of an incorrect response, there will be a mandatory 6-second waiting period to review the correct answer. When your response is correct, feedback will be displayed for 1 second.

           3. A posttest consisting of 60 items will be administered. You will undertake the same task as in the pretest and learning session, but there will be no feedback for your responses.

           4. There will be a brief survey about your learning experience, as well as survey questions related to your demographic information.

Participating in this study is completely voluntary and if you decide to participate now, you may change your mind and stop at any point. You may choose not to answer any survey questions or do the training.

As a participant in this research study, you may gain knowledge about bird categories. The findings of this research may provide recommendations for optimal sequencing of practices in real-world scenarios.

There are no foreseeable risks involved in participating in this study other than those encountered in day-to-day life.

To ensure active participation in the experiment, we have a requirement that you must achieve a minimum of 10% accuracy throughout the entire session to receive the compensation. This means you need to provide at least 27 correct answers out of a total of 268 trials, which includes the pretest, learning session, and posttest. If you do not meet this requirement, your HIT will not be approved. Once you meet this requirement, you will receive a base payment of $10. Furthermore, there is an opportunity for an additional bonus of $0.05 for each correct answer across all phases of the training, including the pretest, learning session, and posttest. For example, if you achieve a total of 100 correct answers, the bonus will amount to $6.

All efforts, within the limits allowed by law, will be made to keep the personal information (your Amazon Turk Worker ID) in your research record private, but total privacy cannot be promised. We will deidentify your data (remove your ID) after the experiment before storing it on our computers long-term. Because of privacy and confidentiality limitations associated with using MTurk IDs, we cannot guarantee complete anonymity. Worker IDs will only be used to distribute payment and will not be stored with survey responses. MTurk Worker IDs will not be shared with anyone. Further identifying information we gather (e.g. demographic information or IP addresses) will never be attached to your responses.

If you have questions about the research you may contact Meng Cao at 901-281-7348 or via email at mcao@memphis.edu and, or Philip Pavlik at 901-678-2326 or via email at ppavlik@memphis.edu. For questions regarding the research subjects' rights, the Chair of the Institutional Review Board for the Protection of Human Subjects should be contacted at 901.678.2705 or via email at irb@memphis.edu.

ELECTRONIC CONSENT

Please select your choice below. You may print a copy of this consent document for your records. Clicking on the Continue button indicates that you:

  • Have read the above information
  • Voluntarily agree to participate
  • Are 18 years of age or older

Welcome to the pretest session, which includes a total of 40 trials. In each trial, you'll be shown an image of a bird. Your task is to correctly identify the bird's category from 11 possible options: Altamira Oriole, Audubon's Oriole, Baltimore Oriole, Bullock's Oriole, Campo Oriole, Hooded Oriole, Orange Oriole, Scott's Oriole, Yellow-backed Oriole, Yellow Oriole, and Spot-breasted Oriole.

Please give your best effort to classify each bird accurately. If you don't know the answer, please make your best guess; your active participation is crucial for the success of this assessment.

Keep in Mind:

This pretest serves as an initial assessment of your bird category knowledge. You'll have a chance to learn these bird categories during the subsequent learning session.

You won't receive feedback on your answers during the pretest.

As a bonus, you'll earn $0.05 for each correct answer.

To promote active engagement in the experiment, Please note that we have a requirement that you must achieve a minimum of 10% correct rate considering the overall correctness throughout the pretest, learning session, and posttest. If you do not meet this requirement, your HIT won't be approved.
